newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Kohl, Klaus sign Czech-German declaration.
newsitem.headline: Kohl, Klaus sign Czech-German declaration.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus on Tuesday signed a joint declaration meant to cement post-war reconciliation between the two neighbours.

In the accord, Bonn expresses its sorrow at the 1938-45 Nazi occupation of Czech lands and Prague its regret at the post-war expulsion of some 2.5 million Sudeten Germans. Germany also backs Czech membership of the European Union and NATO.
"The declaration which we have just signed is a big step forward for both of our nations," Kohl said after the signing in Prague's Liechtenstein Palace.
"We cannot stay in the past or in the end the past will win," Kohl said, adding that the accord would mean better neighbourly relations and peaceful co-existence in Europe.
The two countries also agreed to set up a 160 million mark ($98.6 million) "Future Fund", mainly with German money and intended primarily to benefit victims of Nazi aggression.

The accord, drawn up after two years of delicate talks, is controversial in both countries. Czech far-right Republicans and communists oppose it and relatives and supporters of the Sudeten Germans have also criticised the declaration.
